headline: BIG MISSED (report Oct 26, absent from all prior Oct 28 scans) -- UN Independent International Commission of Inquiry
dek: The commission found Israel 'continuing to commit genocidal acts with the genocidal intent to destroy, in whole or in part, the Palestinians in Gaza' after the US-brokered ceasefire of Oct 2025, rejecting the Board of Peace claim the ceasefire had 'largely held'; between the Oct 10, 2025 ceasefire…
sources: UN Independent International Commission of Inquiry on the Occupied Palestinian Territory, incl. East Jerusalem, and Israel -- report via Reuters (Geneva, Oct 26)
fault_line: Does a UN commission finding of continued genocidal acts after a ceasefire change anything while the war powers and the Board of Peace say the truce 'largely held' -- or is this another report Israel can dismiss?

sections.what_happened: The commission found Israel 'continuing to commit genocidal acts with the genocidal intent to destroy, in whole or in part, the Palestinians in Gaza' after the US-brokered ceasefire of Oct 2025, rejecting the Board of Peace claim the ceasefire had 'largely held'; between the Oct 10, 2025 ceasefire and end-Sep 2026, Israeli strikes/artillery/sniper fire killed 1,431 Palestinians in Gaza including 300 children (TOB/New York Times carry of the report); Israeli territorial control in Gaza expanded from 53% to at least 60% since the ceasefire, with the 'Yellow Line' encroaching and becoming a de facto border; at least 196 Palestinians including 43 children killed along the advancing front (The National); the report also accuses Israeli authorities of crimes against humanity in the West Bank (extermination, persecution, torture, rape and other sexual violence) and faults the Palestinian Authority for targeting dissenting Palestinians. Israel dismissed the report as part of a 'misinformation campaign' (Amb. Daniel Meron, Geneva mission).
sections.what_verified: Report contents carried by Reuters (T1) and AP (T1, via DT Next/Moneycontrol carries); Al Jazeera (T2, STATE QA) independently reports the same findings. The underlying genocide allegation itself remains contested (ICJ South Africa case pending; Israel rejects it) -- the PASS covers reporting the report with attribution and the rejection, not adjudicating genocide as fact.
sections.what_disputed: Israel's Geneva mission: the report is a 'misinformation campaign to demonize the State of Israel' and an attempt to undermine its legitimacy and right to self-defence. AP notes it could not independently corroborate multiple graphic sexual-assault accounts described in the report. The commission's finding is not an ICJ ruling; the South Africa genocide case at the ICJ remains pending.
sections.why_matters: A UN commission says the Gaza ceasefire did not stop the killing: 1,431 dead since the truce, and Israeli control up from 53% to 60% of Gaza. Israel calls it a misinformation campaign. The Yellow Line is the evidence -- it keeps moving.
sections.context: Background: BIG MISSED (report Oct 26, absent from all prior Oct 28 scans) -- UN Independent International Commission of Inquiry: Israel kept committing genocide in Gaza after the Oct 2025 truce; crimes against humanity in the West Bank

totw_analysis: Our read: A UN commission says the Gaza ceasefire did not stop the killing: 1,431 dead since the truce, and Israeli control up from 53% to 60% of Gaza. Israel calls it a misinformation campaign. The Yellow Line is the evidence -- it keeps moving. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Does a UN commission finding of continued genocidal acts after a ceasefire change anything while the war powers and the Board of Peace say the truce 'largely held' -- or is this another report Israel can dismiss?
